title: Against those who say the soul is number
pass_a_gloss: Enough has been shown from many points that the soul is neither entelechy nor ungenerated-in-body in the rejected sense. Pythagoras, accustomed to liken God and all things to numbers, also likened the soul to a self-moving number, and Xenocrates followed him. Not that the soul is a number, but that it is among numbered and pluralized things, discriminating things by imposing forms. Number is a quantity; the soul is not a quantity but a substance — therefore the soul is not a number. Number is discontinuous; the soul is continuous. Number is even or odd; the soul is neither. Number increases by addition; the soul does not. The soul is self-moving; a definite number is unmoved. Number, remaining one and the same in nature, cannot exchange qualities; the soul, remaining one in substance, changes from ignorance to knowledge and from vice to virtue. Therefore the soul is not number.
pass_b_english: Pythagoras loved to speak of God and the world in numbers, and he pictured the soul as a self-moving number; Xenocrates followed. The point is not that soul equals a numeral, but that soul works among countable, many things, sorting them by form. Quantity is what number is; substance is what soul is — so soul is not number. Number breaks into discrete units; soul holds together. Number is even or odd; soul is neither. Add units and number grows; soul does not grow by addition. Soul moves itself; a fixed number does not. A number keeps one nature and cannot trade qualities; the soul stays one substance while passing from ignorance to knowledge and from vice to virtue. Therefore the soul is not number.
